# Prepare a tender response

You work in sales engineering for Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH, a German hydraulics and components manufacturer. Prepare one net EUR bid for Stadt Buchenstadt, Verkehrsbetriebe: Lieferung von Hydraulikzylinder für Werkstatt-Hebeanlagen (VG-2027-7093). The scenario date is 2027-01-25T09:00:00Z; the tender deadline is 2027-02-12T11:00:00Z.

Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer's supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`). The websites are in German; obsolete documents and unrelated records are present.

## Rules

1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.


## Additional rules

These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.

- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
- Finding records: the specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
- Commercial clauses: a tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
- Withdrawn answers: a tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
- Scoped amendments: after selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
- Shared stock: sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
- Conditional discount: the latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
- Units: tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
- Pricing breakdown: base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
- These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
- Technical derivation: for a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
- Authority and time: resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
- Currency: the valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
- Packaging: Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
- Delivery: Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
- Shared setup: Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
- Project bonus: the finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
- Final price: clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
- Metal indices: select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
- Scoring in bid cases: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.

## Site access

- tender-portal: https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run
  Username: `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` · Password: `REDACTED`
- customer-portal: https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run
  Username: `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` · Password: `REDACTED`
- erp: https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run
  Username: `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` · Password: `REDACTED`
- mail: https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run
  Username: `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` · Password: `REDACTED`

## Submission

Submit through the tender portal's "Angebotsabgabe" at https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run, after "Teilnahme bekunden" for this tender. Register the bidder using the company name Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH and USt-IdNr. DE811234567. Choose Hauptangebot for bid or Verzichtserklärung for no_bid. Complete the material configurator, enter the discounted net unit prices and total in German number format, and acknowledge the tender documents. The displayed gross amount includes VAT and is not the required net total. Retrieve the signing TAN from the bidder's webmail, review the summary, and confirm "Angebot verbindlich abgeben" in the browser dialog.

Exactly one submission is allowed; submitting ends the run. Wall-clock time and LLM tokens count toward your result. Unsaved entries are lost when the portal session expires. Going back clears the later steps. A new TAN request invalidates the previous TAN; each TAN is valid for five minutes.

"""The run's browsers: attach over CDP and get a page. Driving them is up to you.

In a run the sandbox starts the browsers (agent.json "browsers": 1 to 4, default 1) before the clock starts and sets
CDP_URL (browser 1) and CDP_URLS (all of them, as a JSON array). Use those: the sandbox stops browsers your agent
starts itself. On your own machine there is no CDP_URLS, so `connect` starts a local Chromium (once:
`uv run playwright install chromium`; HEADLESS=1 hides it). Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md
"""
import json
import os


def cdp_urls(env=os.environ) -> list[str]:
    """Every browser of the run, in order; [] on your own machine."""
    try:
        urls = [url for url in json.loads(env.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]") if isinstance(url, str)]
    except ValueError:
        urls = []
    return urls or ([env["CDP_URL"]] if env.get("CDP_URL") else [])


async def connect(playwright, number: int = 0):
    """Browser `number` of the run (0 is browser 1) and a page in it. Locally, a Chromium of its own."""
    urls = cdp_urls()
    if urls:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.connect_over_cdp(urls[number])

        if self.page.is_closed():
            open_pages = self._open_tabs()
            if open_pages:

                self._watch(self.page)

class Site:
    """One website, driven in its own browser: the active tab, its numbered elements, dialogs, new tabs, downloads.

    Several Sites can share one browser (spawn()): each drives its own tabs, with the same login."""

    def __init__(self, access: dict, context, page, log=print):
        self.access = access
        self.id = access.get("siteId") or urlparse(access["url"]).hostname
        self.url = access["url"]
        self.credentials = access.get("credentials") or {}
        self.context, self.page, self.log = context, page, log
        self.tabs = [page]  # this Site's own tabs, oldest first
        self.acted_at = 0.0  # when this Site last clicked or typed: a popup without an opener is its
        self.refs: dict[int, object] = {}  # element number -> the frame it is in
        self.events: list[str] = []  # dialogs, tabs and downloads since the last view
        self.downloads: list[Path] = []
        self.full_view, self.shown = "", 0
        sites = _SITES.setdefault(id(context), [])
        if not sites:  # one handler per browser hands each new tab to the Site that opened it
            # whether the code is opening a tab is read when the event arrives, before the opening call returns
            context.on("page", lambda tab, key=id(context): _hand_over(key, tab, _OPENING.get(key, 0) > 0))
        sites.append(self)
        self._watch(page)

    async def spawn(self) -> "Site":
        """Another Site on this website in a new tab of the same browser (same login), for an agent working in
        parallel: it starts at the website's start address."""
        page = await self._open_page()
        return Site(self.access, self.context, page, self.log)

    async def _open_page(self):
        key = id(self.context)
        _OPENING[key] = _OPENING.get(key, 0) + 1
        try:
            return await self.context.new_page()
        finally:
            _OPENING[key] -= 1

    # --- events -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _watch(self, page):
        page.on("dialog", self._dialog)
        page.on("download", self._download)

    def _adopt(self, page):
        self._watch(page)
        self.tabs.append(page)
        self.page = page
        self.events.append("A new tab opened and is now the active tab.")

    async def _dialog(self, dialog):
        # Browser dialogs block the page until answered. The agents only trigger them on purpose (the final
        # confirmation of a bid is one), so they are accepted and reported in the next view.
        self.events.append(f"A browser {dialog.type} dialog said {short(dialog.message)!r}; it was accepted.")
        try:
            await dialog.accept()
        except Exception:
            pass

    async def _download(self, download):
        target = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / (download.suggested_filename or "download")
        try:
            await download.save_as(target)
        except Exception as error:
            self.events.append(f"A download failed: {short(error)}")
            return
        self.downloads.append(target)
        self.events.append(f"Downloaded {target.name!r}: read it with read_document(download={len(self.downloads)}).")

    async def keep_alive(self):
        """Loads the current address in the background with this browser's cookies, leaving the page untouched: a
        website that logs out after a short idle time keeps the session while its agent waits."""
        try:
            await self.context.request.get(self.page.url, timeout=8000)
        except Exception:
            pass

class Topics:
    """A mail agent's checklist: each topic is closed only with a message that can apply (the exact reference, dated
    no later than the scenario date, recorded) or after a search of every folder found none. Code checks what it can,
    because in runs #6 and #7 agents finished with look-alike or future-dated messages and topics never searched."""

    def __init__(self, topics: list[dict], reference: str, scenario_date: str, site: web.Site, ledger: Ledger):
        self.topics = {str(t.get("topic", "")).strip(): t for t in topics if str(t.get("topic", "")).strip()}
        self.closed: dict[str, str] = {}
        self.warned: set[tuple] = set()
        self.reference, self.scenario_day = reference, calc.day(scenario_date)
        self.site, self.ledger = site, ledger

    def _topic(self, name: str) -> str | None:
        want = name.strip().lower()
        return next((t for t in self.topics if t.lower() == want), None) or \
            next((t for t in self.topics if want and (want in t.lower() or t.lower() in want)), None)

    def status(self) -> str:
        return "; ".join(f"{t}: {self.closed.get(t, 'OPEN')}" for t in self.topics)

    def open(self) -> list[str]:
        return [t for t in self.topics if t not in self.closed]

    async def close(self, topic: str, outcome: str, reference_as_written: str = "", date: str = "", sender: str = "",
                    subject: str = "", folders_searched: list | None = None) -> str:
        name = self._topic(topic)
        if name is None:
            return f"{topic!r} is not one of your topics: {', '.join(self.topics)}."
        if outcome == "absent":
            folders = {str(f).strip().lower() for f in folders_searched or [] if str(f).strip()}
            if len(folders) < 2:
                return ("Before closing a topic as absent, search it in every folder of the mailbox (inbox, archive "
                        "and any other), also with a shorter or another spelling of the word, and list the folders.")
            self.closed[name] = f"absent (searched {', '.join(sorted(folders))})"
            return f"Closed {name} as absent. Open topics: {', '.join(self.open()) or 'none'}."
        written = str(reference_as_written or subject)
        if self.reference and not re.search(rf"(?<![\w-]){re.escape(self.reference)}(?![\w-]|/\w)", written):
            return (f"{written!r} is not exactly the tender reference {self.reference}: a reference with an added "
                    "suffix or another number is another tender, and its messages never apply. Open the message for "
                    "exactly this reference (other results, other folders), record it, then close the topic.")
        day = calc.day(date)
        if day and self.scenario_day and day > self.scenario_day:
            return (f"That message is dated {date}, after the scenario date {self.scenario_day}: it never applies. "
                    "Open the latest message on this topic dated no later than the scenario date (other results, "
                    "other folders), record it, then close the topic.")
        expected = str(self.topics[name].get("sender") or "").strip().lower()
        if expected and sender and not sender.strip().lower().startswith(expected + "@") \
                and (name, sender) not in self.warned:
            self.warned.add((name, sender))
            return (f"The brief authorizes {expected}@ for {name}; {sender} is another sender, whose message does not "
                    "apply. Look for the message from the authorized sender; if this one is from it after all, close "
                    "the topic again with the same sender.")
        mine = [e for e in self.ledger.entries if e["site"] == self.site.id]
        words = [w for w in (subject, name) if w]
        if not any(w.lower() in json.dumps(e, ensure_ascii=False).lower() for e in mine for w in words):
            return "Record the message (sender, date, subject, reference, its original text) with record() first."
        self.closed[name] = f"{subject or 'message'} of {date or '?'}"
        return f"Closed {name}. Open topics: {', '.join(self.open()) or 'none: call finish'}."

    async def check(self, args: dict) -> str | None:
        """finish() is refused while a topic is open."""
        if self.open():
            return (f"Not yet: these topics are still open: {', '.join(self.open())}. For each: search the exact "
                    "reference with the topic word in every folder, open the latest applicable message, record it, "
                    f"then close_topic(). Checklist: {self.status()}")
        return None

    def tools(self) -> list:
        return [(tool("close_topic", "Close one of your mail topics: with the message you recorded for it (outcome "
                                     "\"recorded\"), or as \"absent\" after searching every folder found none.", {
            "topic": {"type": "string"}, "outcome": {"type": "string", "enum": ["recorded", "absent"]},
            "subject": {"type": "string", "description": "The message's subject, exactly"},
            "reference_as_written": {"type": "string", "description": "The tender reference exactly as the message "
                                                                      "writes it"},
            "date": {"type": "string", "description": "The message's date and time"},
            "sender": {"type": "string", "description": "The sender's address"},
            "folders_searched": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}},
            ["topic", "outcome"]), self.close)]

MAIL_AGENTS = 3  # parallel mail agents at most, each in its own tab with a share of the topics


def topic_groups(topics: list[dict], most: int = MAIL_AGENTS) -> list[list[dict]]:
    """The mail topics dealt out to up to `most` agents, about three each, in the brief's order."""
    topics = [t for t in topics or [] if str(t.get("topic", "")).strip()]
    count = max(1, min(most, len(topics) // 3 + (1 if len(topics) % 3 else 0)))
    return [group for group in (topics[i::count] for i in range(count)) if group]


async def investigate_mail(site: web.Site, task: dict, the_plan: dict, ledger: Ledger, deadline: float):
    """The mailbox, its topics shared among parallel agents in tabs of the same browser: one agent alone ran out of
    time before reaching every topic (runs #6, #7). The first tab logs in before the others open."""
    groups = topic_groups(the_plan.get("mail_topics") or [])
    first_view = await enter(site)
    if len(groups) <= 1:
        return await investigate(site, task, the_plan, ledger, deadline, first_view=first_view,
                                 topics=groups[0] if groups else None)
    tabs = [site]
    for _ in groups[1:]:
        try:
            tabs.append(await site.spawn())
        except Exception as error:
            print(f"[team] another mail tab failed: {error!r}", flush=True)
    if len(tabs) < len(groups):  # fewer tabs than planned: deal the topics out again
        groups = topic_groups(the_plan.get("mail_topics") or [], len(tabs))

    async def one(number: int, tab: web.Site, group: list[dict]):
        view = first_view if tab is site else await enter(tab)
        return await investigate(tab, task, the_plan, ledger, deadline, first_view=view, topics=group,
                                 name=site.id if number == 0 else f"{site.id}-{number + 1}")

    print(f"[team] mail topics: {[[t.get('topic') for t in group] for group in groups]}", flush=True)
    return await asyncio.gather(*(one(number, tab, group) for number, (tab, group) in enumerate(zip(tabs, groups))),
                                return_exceptions=True)

import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

import team  # noqa: E402

TOPICS = [{"topic": "Kursblatt", "sender": "geld", "gives": "exchange rate"},
          {"topic": "Staffelrabatt", "sender": "chef", "gives": "discount"}]


class Checklist(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.ledger = team.Ledger()
        self.site = SimpleNamespace(id="post")
        self.topics = team.Topics(TOPICS, "AB-2030-11", "2030-03-10T09:00:00Z", self.site, self.ledger)

    def close(self, **kwargs) -> str:
        return asyncio.run(self.topics.close(**kwargs))

    def test_finish_is_refused_while_a_topic_is_open(self):
        self.assertIn("Kursblatt", asyncio.run(self.topics.check({})))

    def test_a_look_alike_reference_or_a_later_date_does_not_close_a_topic(self):
        self.ledger.add("post", "/m/1", "mail", {"subject": "Kursblatt AB-2030-11-A"})
        answer = self.close(topic="Kursblatt", outcome="recorded", subject="Kursblatt AB-2030-11-A",
                            reference_as_written="AB-2030-11-A", date="09.03.2030, 10:00", sender="geld@firma.example")
        self.assertIn("not exactly the tender reference", answer)
        answer = self.close(topic="Kursblatt", outcome="recorded", subject="Kursblatt AB-2030-11",
                            reference_as_written="AB-2030-11", date="11.03.2030, 08:00", sender="geld@firma.example")
        self.assertIn("after the scenario date", answer)
        self.assertEqual(self.topics.open(), ["Kursblatt", "Staffelrabatt"])

    def test_a_topic_closes_with_a_recorded_message_that_can_apply(self):
        answer = self.close(topic="kursblatt", outcome="recorded", subject="Kursblatt AB-2030-11",
                            reference_as_written="AB-2030-11", date="09.03.2030, 10:00", sender="geld@firma.example")
        self.assertIn("Record the message", answer)  # nothing recorded yet
        self.ledger.add("post", "/m/2", "mail", {"subject": "Kursblatt AB-2030-11", "rate": "1,1"})
        answer = self.close(topic="kursblatt", outcome="recorded", subject="Kursblatt AB-2030-11",
                            reference_as_written="AB-2030-11", date="09.03.2030, 10:00", sender="geld@firma.example")
        self.assertIn("Closed Kursblatt", answer)
        self.assertEqual(self.topics.open(), ["Staffelrabatt"])

    def test_another_sender_is_questioned_once(self):
        self.ledger.add("post", "/m/3", "mail", {"subject": "Staffelrabatt AB-2030-11"})
        arguments = dict(topic="Staffelrabatt", outcome="recorded", subject="Staffelrabatt AB-2030-11",
                         reference_as_written="AB-2030-11", date="2030-03-01", sender="vertrieb@firma.example")
        self.assertIn("another sender", self.close(**arguments))
        self.assertIn("Closed", self.close(**arguments))

    def test_absent_needs_every_folder(self):
        self.assertIn("every folder", self.close(topic="Kursblatt", outcome="absent", folders_searched=["Eingang"]))
        self.assertIn("Closed Kursblatt as absent",
                      self.close(topic="Kursblatt", outcome="absent", folders_searched=["Eingang", "Archiv"]))

        self.assertEqual(len(team.topic_groups(topics[:3])), 1)

The six analysts are still working, about 25 minutes in. I'll pick up their findings as soon as they finish. Here is where things stand.

**Timing:** the logs have no timestamps, so the only timing I have comes from when each record was saved:

| Run | Total | Tender portal | Spec portal | Mail | ERP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 14.7 min | 0.2–2.3 min | 3.0–5.8 | 0.6 only | 1.3–8.6 |
| 6 | 11.6 min | 1.4–3.8 | 0.9 | 0.7–5.1 | 1.2–7.3 |
| 7 | 14.3 min | 2.0–5.3 | 1.9–4.1 | 2.4–2.9 | 2.7–9.1 |

- **ERP:** this is the slowest part. It took 6–7 minutes in each run, partly because it looked up materials nobody needs (the blocked HZ-8405 and an unused group).
- **Mail:** the agent stops after 1–4 minutes with topics never searched. The follow-up round then has to look again, with its own pass of the solver (the step that turns the records into the price inputs).
- **Start-up:** the first record took up to 2 minutes in run 7.
- I can't yet split the solver, the follow-up and the bid form, because there are no timestamps. The timing analyst is reconstructing those from the step order.

**Built since your last message.** None of this has been through a sandbox run yet; all 54 offline tests pass:

- **Time stamps on every log line**, so the next run shows exactly where the minutes go.
- **Mail split across up to 3 agents in parallel tabs.** The plan step lists the mail topics from the brief, and each agent gets about 3 of them.
- **A topic checklist checked in code.** A topic only closes with a recorded message for the exact reference, dated on or before the scenario date. A look-alike like "-A" or a message dated 26.01 is rejected, and an agent can't finish while any of its topics is still open. Run 7 lost its currency fixing and metal index to exactly these two kinds of decoy.
- **ERP helpers.** The ERP agent can hand each requirement to a helper working in another tab, so the four lookups run at the same time instead of one after another.
- **Tooltip and description text in the page view**, such as the ERP status legend "01 freigegeben · 03 gesperrt" that was hidden in a tooltip.

Still to do once the analysts finish: fixes for the solver and the bid form, an independent review of all changes, and a PITFALLS.md update. Then I'll ask you before starting the one sandbox run.

Yes, there's a lot in it. I opened every team's details: models, token use and run history.

**What the leaderboard shows**

| Rank | Team | Score | Cost | Time | Tokens | Model |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Plite | 100 | $0.087 | 4:41 | 638k | Qwen 3.8 Flash Next (hosted) |
| 2 | isar-labs | 100 | $0.105 | 4:37 | 957k | Qwen 3.8 Flash Next |
| 3 | error404.ai | 100 | $0.110 | 7:33 | 1.2M | Qwen 3.8 Flash Next |
| 4 | AdminRights | 100 | $0.204 | 5:42 | 2.1M | Claude Haiku 5.5 |
| 9 | PolyETHylen | 100 | $1.06 | 14:54 | 7.5M | GPT-6 Luna, plus a little Sol and Clef |
| 10 | BaoByte | 87.9 | $3.46 | 10:24 | 4.2M | GPT-6 Sol |
| **11** | **us** | **71.2** | **$0.51** | **11:33** | **6.9M** | GPT-6 Luna 99% |

**Insights**

1. **A 100 is now the entry ticket.** Nine teams have it, and among them the order follows cost first, then time. QuoteCraft and Here for the Memes cost about the same, and the faster one ranks higher.
2. **The leaders win on efficiency, not on a better model.** Per token, our GPT-6 Luna (~$0.056 per million) is cheaper than hosted Qwen (~$0.14 per million). The leaders use about 10× fewer tokens than we do (638k vs 6.9M) and finish in under 5 minutes, against our 11–14.
3. **PolyETHylen got 100 on its first submission with our setup** (Luna plus a little Sol), so the model isn't what holds us back.
4. **Other teams climbed the same way we are:** 10 → 37 → 80.7 → 100 for Plite, over a few hours.

**Where our tokens and time go:**
- Each page view is up to 16,000 characters and gets sent again with every model step. Run 7 made 468 model calls.
- The investigation runs on a fixed clock: the ERP agent is held until minute 9 and the window closes at 10:30, even when the work is done earlier.
- The bid form takes 37–73 model steps, because the model copies the values by hand.

**Plan (no change to the current order)**

1. **First a reliable ≥90.** The diagnosis confirms that runs 6 and 7 lost almost everything on 4 missing mail facts. The solver analyst replayed run 6's actual records plus those 4 facts and got exactly 100. All six analysts have finished, and the merge into a ranked fix list is running now.
2. **Then speed and cost, which these fixes already help:**
   - stop the investigation as soon as every checklist is complete;
   - have code fill each bid-form row (`enter_position`), so the form takes about 15 steps instead of 50;
   - make the page views smaller and send less history.

The analysis is in its last step: one agent is merging the findings into a ranked fix plan, and should take a few more minutes. Meanwhile I've read the last three reports. Here is what they say:

**Timing.** The 20-minute limit was never the problem. We signed at 14:45, 11:33 and 14:17, leaving 5–8 minutes unused each time.
- **Mail:** the agent stopped at about minute 2–6, even though the currency fixing was still missing.
- **ERP:** it then worked alone until about minute 9, and spent 35–40% of that time on materials no position can use: a blocked one, an unused requirement, and candidates that don't match.
- **Follow-up round:** it recovered no mail fact in any of the three runs. It's a fresh agent with only 75 s, it starts on a stale page, and it searches by codes like FX-6282 that the mailbox search doesn't match.
- **Hidden step cap:** the investigators have a limit of 150 model steps, which can end them minutes early.

**ERP.** No ERP value that reached the solver was wrong; the risk is time.
- In run 7 the active alternative for position 01.01 was found only at minute 9. Until then only the blocked material had been recorded, so a no-bid (about 85 points lost) was one step away.
- The analyst recommends that code, not the model, starts one helper per catalogue group.
- Each helper should get a checklist: a group can't be closed until every candidate's status is recorded.

**Fair play and generalization.** No public values were found in the agent code, but there are some things to clean up:
- remove the "-A" example from a prompt;
- handle an "api" submission;
- don't assume the TAN arrives in the mailbox;
- make calc read "1.000" as a thousand where a whole number is expected.

**What I'm doing next:** once the ranked plan arrives, I'll build the fixes in that order. The top candidates:
1. A gap check while the investigators are still working, so missing facts get fixed during the run rather than after it.
2. Code-driven ERP helpers with a checklist.
3. Bid-form checks per position and of the summary before the TAN.
4. The smaller guards: the step cap, no typing into password fields, a time limit on the solver, and a stricter no-bid rule.

After that comes an independent review of the code, the tests, the fair-play check and the PITFALLS.md update. Then I'll ask you before starting the one sandbox run.

                 refusals: int = 2, news=None, warn_at: float = 0.0, warning: str = "",
                 hard_deadline: float = float("inf")):
        self.name, self.system, self.deadline, self.effort = name, system, deadline, effort
        self.hard_deadline = hard_deadline  # never answered after this, whatever happens (the submission waits)
        self.check = check  # finish() is refused while check(arguments) names a problem
        self.stay_until, self.refusals, self.max_refusals = stay_until, 0, refusals

        self.warn_at, self.warning = warn_at, warning  # one message at warn_at, e.g. to wrap up before the end
        self.schemas = [schema for schema, _ in tools]

        """One line per record of the other agents, oldest first: what the team knows, at a glance. Long enough per
        record to carry its identifiers (a requirement's catalogue group sits after its attributes); when it is too
        long in all, the newest records are kept."""
        lines = [f"#{entry['n']} [{entry['agent']}] {entry['topic']}: "

                   and entry["agent"] != exclude_agent]

DATE_KEYS = re.compile(r"date|datum|sent|gesendet|received|empfangen|zeit|time", re.I)


def record_days(facts) -> list[str]:
    """The calendar days in a record's date fields (keys named like a date), not dates inside its text."""
    days = []
    if isinstance(facts, dict):
        for key, value in facts.items():
            if isinstance(value, (dict, list)):
                days += record_days(value)
            elif DATE_KEYS.search(str(key)) and calc.day(value):
                days.append(calc.day(value))
    elif isinstance(facts, list):
        for value in facts:
            days += record_days(value)
    return days


class Topics:
    """A mail agent's checklist: each topic is closed only with a recorded message that can apply (the exact
    reference, dated no later than the scenario date) or as absent once its search trail shows the word searched.
    Code checks what it can, because in runs #6 and #7 agents finished with look-alike or future-dated messages,
    transliterated search words and topics never searched. Each check refuses at most twice per topic, so a site the
    checks do not fit cannot trap the agent."""

    def __init__(self, topics: list[dict], reference: str, scenario_date: str, site: web.Site, ledger: Ledger,
                 agent: str | None = None):
        self.topics = {str(t.get("topic", "")).strip(): t for t in topics if str(t.get("topic", "")).strip()}
        self.closed: dict[str, str] = {}
        self.refused: dict[str, int] = {}
        self.warned: set[tuple] = set()
        self.reference, self.scenario_day = reference, calc.day(scenario_date)
        self.site, self.ledger, self.agent = site, ledger, agent or site.id
        self.trail_start = len(site.trail) if hasattr(site, "trail") else 0

    def _topic(self, name: str) -> str | None:
        want = fold(name.strip())
        return next((t for t in self.topics if fold(t) == want), None) or \\
            next((t for t in self.topics if want and (want in fold(t) or fold(t) in want)), None)

    def status(self) -> str:
        return "; ".join(f"{t}: {self.closed.get(t, 'OPEN')}" for t in self.topics)

    def open(self) -> list[str]:
        return [t for t in self.topics if t not in self.closed]

    def _refuse(self, name: str, text: str) -> str | None:
        """The refusal, or None once this topic was refused twice (the checks may not fit this website)."""
        self.refused[name] = self.refused.get(name, 0) + 1
        return text if self.refused[name] <= 2 else None

    def _close(self, name: str, how: str) -> str:
        self.closed[name] = how
        return f"Closed {name}. Open topics: {', '.join(self.open()) or 'none: call finish'}."

    def _searched(self, word: str) -> tuple[int, bool]:
        """How often the trail shows the word searched (distinct addresses, or typed searches), and whether it shows
        only a transliterated spelling."""
        trail = list(getattr(self.site, "trail", []))[self.trail_start:]
        want, plain = fold(word), transliterated(word)
        addresses = {entry for entry in trail if entry.startswith("http") and want in fold(entry)}
        typed = [entry for entry in trail if not entry.startswith("http") and want in fold(entry)]
        wrong = plain != want and any(plain in fold(entry) for entry in trail)
        return max(len(addresses), len(typed)), wrong

    def _suffixed(self, text: str) -> bool:
        """The tender reference appears in the text, and every time with something added (another tender)."""
        if not self.reference:
            return False
        occurrences = [match.end() for match in re.finditer(re.escape(self.reference), text)]
        return bool(occurrences) and all(re.match(r"[-_/.]?[A-Za-z0-9]", text[end:]) for end in occurrences)

                    subject: str = "", folders_searched: list | None = None) -> str:
        name = self._topic(topic)
        if name is None:
            return f"{topic!r} is not one of your topics: {', '.join(self.topics)}."
        if outcome == "absent":
            count, wrong = self._searched(name)
            if count < 2:
                problem = self._refuse(name, (
                    f"The brief spells it {name!r}: your searches used another spelling (the search matches words "
                    f"literally). Search {name!r} exactly, with the exact reference, in every folder." if wrong else
                    f"Your searches do not show {name!r} searched in each folder yet: search the exact reference "
                    f"with {name!r} in every folder of the mailbox (and a shorter form of the word), then close it."))
                if problem:

            folders = ", ".join(str(f) for f in folders_searched or []) or "the folders"
            return self._close(name, f"absent (searched {folders})")
        mine = [e for e in self.ledger.entries if e.get("agent", e["site"]) == self.agent]
        words = [fold(w) for w in (subject, name) if w]
        matching = [e for e in mine if any(w in fold(json.dumps(e, ensure_ascii=False)) for w in words)]
        if not matching:

        written = str(reference_as_written or subject)

                "with something added or another number is another tender, and its messages never apply. Open the "
                "message for exactly this reference (other results, other folders), record it, then close the topic."))
            if problem:

        if self.scenario_day and any(d > self.scenario_day for d in days):
            problem = self._refuse(name, (

                "record it, then close the topic."))
            if problem:

    """The plan's mail topics that would fill the gaps: by the kind of input they give, or by the topic word the
    solver named for a missing mailbox fact. Each with what to tell the agent."""
    topics = the_plan.get("mail_topics") or []
    found: dict[str, tuple[dict, str]] = {}
    for gap in code_gaps(inputs):
        for topic in topics:
            if topic.get("feeds") == gap["feeds"]:
                found.setdefault(fold(topic["topic"]), (topic, gap["fact"]))
    for gap in (inputs or {}).get("missing") or []:
        word = fold(gap.get("topic") or "")
        topic = next((t for t in topics if word and (fold(t["topic"]) == word or fold(t["topic"]) in word)), None)
        if topic:
            seen = f" (seen and rejected: {gap['seen']})" if gap.get("seen") else ""
            found.setdefault(fold(topic["topic"]), (topic, f"{gap.get('fact', '')}{seen}"))
    return list(found.values())

"""The agent loop against a stub model: time limits, not step counts, end an investigator, and nothing a model does
keeps the solver past the moment the submission must start."""
import asyncio
import sys
import time
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import llm  # noqa: E402


def reply(*calls):
    return SimpleNamespace(choices=[SimpleNamespace(message=SimpleNamespace(content="", tool_calls=list(calls)))])


class Loop(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_an_investigator_works_until_its_deadline_not_a_step_count(self):
        async def chat(messages, tools=None, effort="none"):
            return reply(llm._Call(f"c{len(messages)}", "look", "{}"))

        async def look() -> str:
            return "a page"

        agent = llm.Agent("test", "system", [(llm.tool("look", "Look.", {}), look)], deadline=time.time() + 1.0)
        with patch.object(llm, "chat", chat):
            started = time.time()
            asyncio.run(agent.run("task", max_steps=100000))
        self.assertGreater(agent.steps, 150)  # the old cap would have stopped it here
        self.assertLess(time.time() - started, 3)

    def test_the_solver_never_answers_after_its_hard_deadline(self):
        async def chat(messages, tools=None, effort="none"):
            await asyncio.sleep(60)  # reasoning that never ends

        agent = llm.Agent("solver", "system", [], deadline=time.time() + 1, effort="medium",
                          hard_deadline=time.time() + 8)
        with patch.object(llm, "chat", chat):
            started = time.time()
            self.assertIsNone(asyncio.run(agent.run("task", max_steps=4)))
        self.assertLess(time.time() - started, 8)

    def test_a_refused_finish_says_its_summary_is_not_saved(self):
        async def record(topic: str = "", facts=None) -> str:
            return "Recorded."

        agent = llm.Agent("test", "system", [(llm.tool("record", "Save.", {}), record)], deadline=time.time() + 60,
                          stay_until=time.time() + 60, refusals=1)
        answer = asyncio.run(agent._call("finish", '{"summary": "the rate is 1.1"}'))
        self.assertTrue(answer.startswith("Your finish summary is not saved"), answer)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
EOF

  name: 'review-fixes-round-8',

investigates 4 German websites (tender portal, supplier/spec portal, ERP, webmail), computes a bid in code, and signs
it in the tender portal's bid form with a TAN from the webmail. Last sandbox runs scored 71.2 and 67.3; nearly all
lost points came from mail topics never recorded (currency fixing, setup pool, metal index, bonus). The goal of this
round is >= 90 on the next single sandbox run while staying generic for a private dataset (no public values or
site-specific labels in agent code).

Code: /Users/youssefabdelaal/HackathonFinal/agent/{agent.py,team.py,llm.py,web.py,submit.py,calc.py,prompts.py}
Tests: /Users/youssefabdelaal/HackathonFinal/agent/tests/ (70 pass: uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests,
run from the agent directory; you may run them, and you may write throwaway scripts ONLY under
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-youssefabdelaal-HackathonFinal/ef3779ad-38c0-4446-8452-f5fba5854ada/scratchpad/review/)
Evidence of how the real sites behave: /Users/youssefabdelaal/HackathonFinal/notes/site-map-public-1.md,
notes/facts-public-1.md, notes/expected-public-1.json, and real run logs /Users/youssefabdelaal/HackathonFinal/out/
final-run6-d4e4.log, final-run7-8389.log, sandbox-run-8389.check.log (tool calls cut at 200 chars; "browser N:" lines
are the platform's record of clicks/typing). Brief: "/Users/youssefabdelaal/b2b tourism/ehl-hackathon/notes/brief-public-1.md".
PITFALLS: /Users/youssefabdelaal/HackathonFinal/PITFALLS.md.

What changed this round (none of it has run on the live sites yet):
1. Mail: plan lists mail_topics (snapped to the brief's spelling, "Subject/sender" pairs added: team.plan_topics);
   investigate_mail splits topics over up to 3 agents in tabs of one browser (web.Site.spawn, _hand_over, _OPENING);
   team.Topics checklist with close_topic (checks reference suffix, date vs scenario date, sender, search trail
   web.Site.trail for "absent", refusals capped per topic and check kind); finish refused while topics open.
2. Gap rounds during the investigation (team.gap_rounds, code_gaps, gap_topics): a low-effort solve when the mail job
   ends or at until-210 s; a fresh mail agent per missing topic (team.follow_up rebuilt: spawned tab, enter(), the
   site's extra, topics checklist). agent.work: follow-up sized by slack, ledger.latest_inputs fallback.
3. Submission guard (submit.FormGuard): wrapped click refuses once to leave a position step whose fields hold another
   row or miss values; get_tan refuses once while the summary differs from the bid; check_summary tool; confirmed()

   password fields, select fallback via choose_option (+ "none" word matching), off-host goto guard, keep_sessions.

6. ERP delegate(): dedupe by keys, helper starts at the lead's URL, HELPER_TASKS cancelled at the hard stop; ledger

Report only real defects or real risks with a concrete failure scenario (inputs/state -> wrong behaviour), with

minor), and a concrete fix. Do not report style. Check claims by reading the code (and running small scripts) before
reporting. Prefer fewer, solid findings.`

const FINDINGS = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      title: { type: 'string' }, file_line: { type: 'string' },
      severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['critical', 'major', 'minor'] },
      scenario: { type: 'string', description: 'concrete inputs/state -> wrong behaviour' },
      evidence: { type: 'string', description: 'code quotes, script output, log lines' },
      fix: { type: 'string' } },
      required: ['title', 'file_line', 'severity', 'scenario', 'evidence', 'fix'] } },
    summary: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['findings', 'summary'],
}

const VERDICT = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    real: { type: 'boolean' }, severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['critical', 'major', 'minor', 'none'] },
    reasoning: { type: 'string' }, better_fix: { type: 'string' } },
  required: ['real', 'severity', 'reasoning'],
}

const LENSES = [
  { key: 'async', prompt: 'LENS: asyncio lifecycle and concurrency. Tasks created and never awaited or cancelled, exceptions swallowed or crashing investigate_all/work, anything that can hang past deadlines or delay the submission (gap_rounds sleeping, helpers, keeper task, login lock held during reload, _hand_over races with spawn/fresh_tab, Playwright event handler coroutines), several Site objects sharing one context (refs, trail, events, secrets), shared mutable state (HELPER_TASKS module-level, _SITES never cleaned).' },
  { key: 'mail', prompt: 'LENS: the mail topic machinery. Walk the public scenario: which topics the plan + plan_topics yield, how topic_groups splits them, what each agent sees, and whether Topics.close accepts the right messages and refuses decoys using the real record shapes in the run logs (dates like "26.01.2027 10:00 (01/26 MM/DD 2027)", "24.01.2027, 20:00", records as strings not dicts, records cut, subjects shared by decoy and real message, the discount approval whose newest message from the director may not be an approval). Can a correct close be refused forever, can an agent be trapped, can gap_topics route a gap to the wrong topic (augmented topics have feeds "other")? Is the trail check sound with the real search URLs?' },
  { key: 'submit', prompt: 'LENS: the submission path, which signed perfectly in run 6 and must not get worse. FormGuard.step_position/step_problem/summary_problems against what the real bid form shows (site map section 3: steps per position in shuffled order, configurator selects applied with a button that reloads, material select, quantity, price, Preisaufbau details with base/surcharge/packaging/rebate, lead select 1-52 weeks; review page with Prüfpunkt sections in shuffled order and gross amount incl. VAT). Look for false refusals that cost a TAN or minutes, wrong position detection (dates, prices, 01.01 vs 1.01, ids in progress bars), the wrapped click using a stale full_view, get_tan refusing after the TAN was already requested, secrets, choose_option none-word regex false matches, _select fallback picking a wrong option.' },
  { key: 'flow', prompt: 'LENS: agent.work orchestration, solver, calc. The no_bid override logic, follow_up_questions, follow-up sizing vs submit_by, latest_inputs fallback, solver hard_deadline and the patient timeout for tool-less agents (plan agent at effort low), keep_sessions excluding the submission browser, api submission path (main() then submits), tan_site, compute with partial inputs. calc.whole/tagged/stamp: any regression on the public expected answer or on plausible private formats (e.g. quantities like "1.5", prices "1.000,50", price units "1000", dates without time). Verify by running small scripts against calc.' },
  { key: 'general', prompt: 'LENS: generalization to a private dataset and fair play. New assumptions in code or prompts that would break on other websites (search UIs without the query in the URL, a mailbox with one folder, briefs without a Subject/sender list, positions numbered "1", "2", a bid form on one page, TAN delivered elsewhere), any public value or site-specific label added to agent/ code, prompts or tests, and any prompt text that steers the model to public answers. Also check that helpers stay model-directed (the brief forbids code that autonomously discovers and traverses the websites).' },
  { key: 'trace', prompt: 'LENS: an end-to-end mental run of the public scenario with the new code, minute by minute: plan, logins, 3 mail tabs plus gap rounds, ERP lead plus helpers, tender and spec agents, investigation end, solve, follow-up, compute, submission with the guard, TAN. Estimate model calls and wall-clock per phase from the run logs (about 3-4 s per model step), check the deadlines line up (INVESTIGATE_UNTIL, SOLVE_SECONDS, SUBMIT_RESERVE, gap round timing until-210, follow-up 75-210 s) and that signing reliably happens before the end. Report anything that makes the run late, unsigned, much more expensive, or that leaves a scored field empty.' },
]

phase('Review')
const results = await pipeline(
  LENSES,
  (lens) => agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\n${lens.prompt}`, { label: `review:${lens.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS }),
  (review, lens) => parallel((review?.findings || []).map((finding) => () =>
    agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\nA reviewer (lens: ${lens.key}) reported this finding. Try hard to REFUTE it by reading the code,
running small scripts if useful, and checking the evidence. Default to real=false if the scenario cannot actually
happen, is already handled, or is not worth a change before the next run. If it is real, give the severity you
believe and a better fix if you see one.\n\nFINDING:\n${JSON.stringify(finding, null, 1)}`,
      { label: `verify:${lens.key}:${finding.title.slice(0, 40)}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT })
      .then((verdict) => ({ lens: lens.key, ...finding, verdict })))),
)
const all = results.flat().filter(Boolean)
const confirmed = all.filter((f) => f.verdict && f.verdict.real)
log(`${all.length} findings, ${confirmed.length} confirmed`)
return { confirmed, rejected: all.filter((f) => !(f.verdict && f.verdict.real)).map((f) => ({ lens: f.lens, title: f.title, why: f.verdict ? f.verdict.reasoning : 'no verdict' })) }

### Diagnosis of runs #5–#7 (six analysts plus a synthesis) and what was built for run #8

Findings, checked against the logs, the score breakdowns and the hand-checked answer:

- **Nearly every point lost in runs #6 and #7 is a mail fact never recorded.** The solver and `calc.py` are correct:
  replaying the logged run-6 and run-7 inputs with only the missing mail facts added gives exactly 100. The value of
  each fact, all else right: currency fixing about 20, metal index about 23, setup pool about 18, bonus bands about 13.
- **Time was never the limit.** The runs signed after 11.5–14.7 of 20 minutes. The mail agent quit 4.5–7 minutes
  before its window closed, because `finish` was accepted after 4 generic refusals. The ERP worked alone until about
  minute 9.
- **Coverage per topic:**
  - The currency fixing was missed in all three runs: it is archive-only, next to a future-dated decoy with the same
    subject.
  - Decoys found first ended a topic (a look-alike reference, a later date).
  - A transliterated search word found nothing, 12 times in a row.
- **The 75-second follow-up recovered no mail fact in 3 of 3 runs.** It had no site instructions, started on a stale or
  dead-end page, searched key codes in the inbox only, and had no login check.
- **ERP:** no wrong value reached the solver, but 35–40% of its time went to blocked, unused or non-matching
  materials. In run #7 the active alternative to a blocked first hit came at about minute 9, so a wrong no_bid was one
  step away.
- **Investigators had a hidden cap of 150 model steps**, where refused finishes count as steps.
- **The submitter is unreliable:**
  - Run #5 signed with a position omitted and a total that still included it.
  - Run #7 entered one position's row on another's step and skipped fields, and requested 3 TANs.
  - Run #6 was perfect.
- **The platform log loses the first 2–3 minutes of agent output.** It also had no timestamps.

Built (all offline-tested; real run-6 and run-7 records replayed through the checks; nothing run on the live sites
yet):

| Fix | What it does | Fails open how |
|---|---|---|
| Mail topics from the brief | The plan lists every mail topic in the brief's own spelling (a transliterated word is snapped back) and adds every "Subject/sender" pair the brief lists | Unknown words are kept, at most 12 topics |
| Parallel mail tabs | Up to 3 mail agents, about 3 topics each, in tabs of one browser; each tab keeps its own popups | Fewer tabs: topics dealt out again |
| Topic checklist in code | `close_topic` refuses a look-alike reference (its own record shows it), a message dated after the scenario date, an unrecorded message, and "absent" when the search trail does not show the word searched (in two places); `finish` is refused while topics are open | Each check refuses a topic at most twice |
| Gap rounds during the investigation | When the mail agents are done (or 3.5 min before the end): a quick solve; inputs the rules need but that are still empty (foreign currency without rate, masses without index, pool without fee, bonus members without bands, groups without scope) send a fresh mail agent after the matching topic | At most 2 rounds; nothing after the window |
| Follow-up rebuilt | New tab, login, the site's own instructions, the mail checklist for the missing topics; length from the slack (75–210 s) | Bounded by the submission start |
| Submission guard | Before a step is left: does it hold its own row, completely (0,00 included)? Before the TAN: does the summary show each position's material and unit price and the right net total? | One refusal per problem, silent when the layout does not fit, never under 150 s |
| no_bid check | A no_bid stands only if a second look at the candidate list of the group confirms it | Bid with the material empty otherwise |
| ERP helpers | `delegate()` per requirement: deduplicated, starting where the lead is, stopped at the hard stop; logins serialized per browser | At most 3 helpers |
| Safety | Solver hard deadline; investigators bounded by time (400 steps); no typing into password fields via `fill()`; no made-up hosts; keep-alive between phases; select by option text | — |
| Private-data guards | api submission returns the answer; TAN site from the plan; TANs without digits; counts like "1.000"; the condition's number format; ISO times with offsets | Public answer unchanged (re-verified) |
| Logging | Elapsed time on every line, schedule repeated at the end, one compact line per record, exit reason per agent, first line of key tool results | — |

Watch in run #8's log:
- `[team] mail topics` should list all of the brief's topics.
- Each mail agent's `topics:` line should show every topic closed with a real message, not "absent".
- `[team] gap check` should show no gaps, or gaps that a `mail+N` agent then filled.
- Look for `[submit] step check` and `summary check` refusals, and whether they were right.
- `stopped:` lines should give each agent's exit reason.
- Check whether three mail tabs and ERP helpers work side by side: locks, sessions, 503s, model stalls.

Right now I'm waiting on a code review, and I've just finished updating PITFALLS.md.

**Done this round.** All 8 fixes from the ranked plan are built, with 70 offline tests passing:

1. A code-checked mail topic checklist, with up to 3 mail agents searching in parallel tabs.
2. A gap check during the investigation that sends a fresh mail agent after each missing fact. The follow-up round is rebuilt to start in a fresh tab.
3. A bid-form guard that checks each position step, and the summary before the TAN.
4. Safety limits: a hard deadline for the solver, investigators bounded by time instead of 150 steps, no typing into password fields, no made-up hosts.
5. A no-bid only stands if a second look at the materials confirms it.
6. ERP helpers that look up requirements in parallel tabs, and one login per browser at a time.
7. Guards for the private dataset, such as an api submission or the TAN arriving elsewhere. The public answer is unchanged, re-checked to the cent.
8. Timestamps and clearer log lines.

I also replayed the real run 6 and 7 records through the new checks. They catch exactly the decoys and gaps that cost us points. The fair-play check is clean.

**Running now.** Six independent reviewers are going through all the changes, each from one angle:
- async bugs and hangs;
- the mail logic on real record shapes;
- the bid form, which must not get worse than run 6's perfect signing;
- the run flow and calc;
- generalization and fair play;
- a minute-by-minute walk through a full run against the deadlines.

A skeptic then tries to refute each finding, so I only fix real ones. They started a few minutes ago and nothing is back yet.

**After that:**
1. Fix the confirmed findings, then re-run the tests and the fair-play check.
2. Ask you before starting the single sandbox run.

can the choose of the model be the reason we are not scoring good?

Mostly no. The evidence points to how the agent is organised, not to how capable the model is.

**Evidence that the model isn't the main problem:**
- **Same model, 100 points:** PolyETHylen scored 100 on its first submission with GPT-6 Luna, plus a little Sol, which is our setup.
- **Smaller models score 100:** the top 3 teams use hosted Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, and AdminRights uses Claude Haiku 5.5. None of these is stronger than Luna.
- **A bigger model alone didn't do it:** BaoByte uses GPT-6 Sol for everything and has 87.9 at $3.46, almost 7× our cost.
- **The diagnosis:** our solver (Sol) and calc.py were exactly right. Replaying runs 6 and 7 with the 4 missing mail facts gives 100. The facts were missing because the mail agent could stop after 4 refusals with minutes left, took the first decoy it found, and searched a misspelled word. That's orchestration, which is what this round fixes in code.

**Where the model does show up:**
- Luna at low effort makes judgment slips: opening the first hit (a decoy), transliterating "ü" to "ue", and putting a row on the wrong form step. Each of these is now caught by a code check rather than left to the model.
- The submitter runs at effort "none". If the bid-form guard still sees row mix-ups in this run, raising it to "low" is a cheap next step.

A stronger model would mainly raise cost and time, and those decide the ranking among the teams already at 100.

The run is still in the investigation phase; I'll report as events come in.

The ERP lead did start helpers at about 3:12, so the parallel lookups are running. One of them, though, got the wrong job:

| Helper | Job | Correct? |
|---|---|---|
| erp-2 | A-2, group GR-5152 | ✓ |
| erp-3 | A-4, group GR-6617 | ✓ |
| erp-4 | A-5, "group GR-7334, 40 mm / 60 mm / 160 bar / Gelenkkopf / CE, 3 pieces per set" | ✗ The spec agent recorded A-5 as GR-4287 (125/300/250 bar, flange, 5 per set). |

The lead wrote that job itself. I can't find GR-7334 anywhere else in the log so far; it may come from a superseded revision inside a long record, or the model made it up. A-5 is position 01.05 (130 pieces, the largest line), so this matters.

**How it can still recover:**
1. The lead or the helper notices the mismatch with the spec records.
2. If not, the solver sees no material for A-5 and leans to no-bid. The new no-bid guard then sends an ERP follow-up for "every material of group GR-4287", and solves again.
3. Worst case: we bid with 01.05's material empty and lose about 10 of that position's 13 points, since its quantity still scores.

**Fix for next round:** a helper's job will be checked against the specification records before it starts: its group key has to appear in a requirement record from another agent. I'm keeping watch.

content.text:
My estimate is **about 85, with a range of 68–100**. It's mostly pinned down already, with two open risks:

**Secured so far (about 75–80 points' worth looks safe):**
- All 9 mail facts are on the correct messages. That covers the discount, the currency fixing (base prices of the 3 USD positions), the setup pool, the metal index and the bonus. These alone lost about 29 points per run before.
- The tender quantities, the withdrawn answer and the requirements were all recorded correctly.

**Risk 1: position 01.01 may get the blocked material.** The ERP lead recorded the blocked HZ-8405 as "01 freigegeben" (released). I suspect it read the status legend from the tooltip text the page view now shows ("01 freigegeben · 03 gesperrt") as the status itself. If the solver picks HZ-8405 over HZ-1609, we lose about 9 points on 01.01 plus the 5 for the total. I'd call that roughly a coin flip.

**Risk 2: position 01.05 has no correct lookup yet.** The helper got the wrong group (GR-7334). The rescue path is the no-bid guard plus the ERP follow-up asking for group GR-4287; the follow-ups did recover ERP facts in runs 5 and 6. I'd put about a 70% chance it ends up right. If not: about 11 points on 01.05, plus the index-window check and the bonus split.

| Outcome | Score | Rough chance |
|---|---|---|
| Both risks resolve | 95–100 | ~35% |
| 01.01 wrong material only | ~85 | ~35% |
| 01.05 left without a material only | ~78 | ~15% |
| Both go wrong | ~68 | ~15% |

That adds up to an expected score around 85. The new bid-form guard is also untested live and could cost a point or two.

Two fixes for the next round:
- Check that a helper's catalogue group appears in a specification record from another agent before the helper starts.
- Make the prompt say clearly that a legend or tooltip explains the status codes, and that the value shown next to the material is the status.

I'll confirm both risks from the final ledger and score.

### Run #8 (`run_86e8c173d8488a04`): quality 91.8, 15:42 min, $0.50

What worked:
- **Mail: 9 of 9 topics on the right messages by minute 2:06**, from three parallel tabs. This includes the
  archive-only currency fixing next to its future-dated decoy, and the exact price index next to its look-alike.
- **Gap checks** (2:12 and 7:14) found nothing missing.
- **The follow-up worked.** The solver rejected one message whose subject the agent had copied with a typo. A fresh
  `mail+` agent re-read it with the right subject in 29 seconds, and the second solve used it.
- **ERP:** the helpers found 2 of the 4 needed materials in parallel; all four were complete by about minute 5
  (minute 9 in run #7).
- **Every field of 4 of 5 positions was right.** So were the discount, withdrawn answer and index window, and the
  summary check caught a wrong total before the TAN.

| Went wrong in run #8 | Effect | Next fix |
|---|---|---|
| **The ERP lead recorded a price it never opened** ("HZ price" while on another material's page; repeating-digit numbers) after being refused 28 times with "not yet" | 01.01 base and unit price wrong, and the total: 8.25 points | `record()` checks that the identifiers it names appear on the page on screen (refuses once, asks to open that record's page); refusals stop after a few in a row bring no new record |
| The lead delegated one requirement with a made-up catalogue group and attributes (found nowhere in the records) | One helper wasted; the lead covered it itself by luck | `delegate()` refuses a job whose group key does not appear in another agent's record |
| The ERP lead first recorded the blocked material as "01 released" (it took the status legend in the tooltip for the value), and corrected it later | Could have cost a position | prompt: a legend explains the codes; the value shown next to the record is the status |
| The step guard took a lead-time dropdown ("3 Wochen") for a missing value, on all 5 steps | 5 needless refusals; the model read them as form validation errors and tried to give up | read the leading number of a dropdown text |
| The submitter took the form's shuffled position order for an error and tried to finish as "failed" 6 times; the refusal text then listed "summary" problems on a step page | Minutes lost; nearly unsigned | summary check only on the signing page; refusal: "the order is shuffled, each step names its position"; any problem the form cannot fix: sign anyway (a signed bid with an error scores, an unsigned one scores nothing); submitter at effort low |
| The submitter typed one position's line total as the order's net total; caught only at the summary, then a loop of 8 minutes until it found the way back | Nearly unsigned | check the total field on the conditions step before it is left (the guard knows the entered total) |
| configure(): the apply button reloaded the page during the fallback click, and the timeout aborted the chain | 25 s, one retry | treat a fallback-click timeout during navigation as applied and continue |
| The ERP lead stayed refused until minute 9 although done at about minute 7 | 2–3 minutes and tokens | the no-progress cap above ends it; then the investigation ends early |

content.text:
**Run #8 scored 91.8 of 100**, above the 90 you asked for. It's our best: run 6 had 71.2, run 7 had 67.3.

| | Run 7 | Run 8 |
|---|---|---|
| Score | 67.3 | **91.8** |
| Mail facts found | 6 of 9 | **9 of 9** (by minute 2) |
| Positions fully right | 0 of 5 | **4 of 5** |
| Time / cost | 14:17 / $0.43 | 15:42 / $0.50 |

**The 8.2 lost points have a single cause.** The ERP agent recorded a price for position 01.01's material without ever opening its price page. It had been told "not yet" 28 times, and it seems to have invented one to get past that. That one wrong price cost 01.01's base and unit price (3.25) and the correct total (5). Everything else got full marks.

**Near misses, all in the bid form:**
- My new guard falsely flagged the lead-time dropdowns.
- The submitter took the form's shuffled position order for an error, typed one line total as the order total, and looped for about 8 minutes before fixing it. It signed with 4 minutes to spare.
- The summary check did catch the wrong total before the TAN.

**Next fixes**, already in PITFALLS.md:
1. `record()` refuses a fact whose identifiers aren't on the page on screen, and the refusals stop when an agent is clearly done. That fixes the invented price and saves 2–3 minutes.
2. The guard reads "3 Wochen" as 3, and checks the total on its own step.
3. Problems the form can't fix lead to "sign anyway", never to a loop.
4. `delegate()` only accepts catalogue groups that appear in another agent's records.

With these, the same run would have scored 100 and finished faster.

The code review workflow is still running (13 of 21 checks done). I'll fold its confirmed findings into the next round.

Do you want me to promote run #8 (91.8) to the leaderboard? We're currently listed with 71.2. I won't do it without your OK. And should I build the next fixes now and then ask you before another run?
make sure it will get 100 percent

Here is the plan for 100. Run #8 lost points in exactly one place, and nearly lost everything in the bid form. So the next round fixes those causes in code, folds in what the code reviewers confirm, then gets an independent check before a single run. Starting with the invented price, the costliest problem: `record()` will refuse values that never appeared on any page the agent has seen.

async def follow_up_round(task: dict, the_plan: dict, ledger: team.Ledger, inputs: dict | None, by_id: dict,
                          submit_by: float) -> dict | None:
    """One targeted look for the facts the solver found missing, then a second solve. A no_bid stands only when the
    second solve, after a fresh look at the candidate list, agrees, or when the materials were checked and there is
    no time to look again."""
    questions = follow_up_questions(inputs, the_plan, by_id)
    no_bid_first, confirmed = bool(inputs and inputs.get("decision") == "no_bid"), False
    if questions and time.time() + 75 + 30 < submit_by:

        log(f"[team] following up for {seconds:.0f} s on {questions}")

        mail_topics = [topic for topic, _ in team.gap_topics(inputs, the_plan)]
        try:  # a follow-up stuck on a page must never hold up the submission
            await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.gather(*(
                team.follow_up(by_id[site_id], task, the_plan, ledger, asked, until,
                               topics=mail_topics if kind_of(the_plan, site_id) == "mail" and mail_topics else None)
                for site_id, asked in questions.items()), return_exceptions=True), seconds + 30)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            log("[team] the follow-up round did not end in time; going on with what is recorded")
        second = await safely("solve", team.solve(task, the_plan, ledger, min(time.time() + SOLVE_SECONDS, submit_by),
                                                  submit_by))
        confirmed = bool(no_bid_first and second and second.get("decision") == "no_bid")
        inputs = second or inputs
    elif no_bid_first:
        confirmed = materials_checked(inputs, ledger, the_plan)
    if inputs and inputs.get("decision") == "no_bid" and not confirmed:
        # a no_bid that a second look at the materials did not confirm is not trusted (a wrong no_bid loses nearly
        # everything): the known positions are bid, a missing material left empty
        log(f"[team] no_bid not confirmed by a second look at the materials: bidding instead "
            f"({inputs.get('decision_reason')})")
        inputs["decision"] = "bid"
    return inputs


def materials_checked(inputs: dict, ledger: team.Ledger, the_plan: dict) -> bool:
    """Every position left without a material has its catalogue group in a record of the materials website."""
    materials = {s["site_id"] for s in the_plan.get("sites", []) if s.get("kind") == "erp"}
    records = " ".join(json.dumps(entry, ensure_ascii=False) for entry in ledger.entries if entry["site"] in materials)
    groups = [(position.get("requirement") or {}).get("catalogue_group") for position in inputs.get("positions") or []
              if not position.get("material_number")]
    return bool(groups) and all(group and group in records for group in groups)


async def safely(what: str, job, fallback=None):
    """The job's result, or the fallback when it fails: one error must not cost the whole bid."""
    try:

    except Exception as error:
        log(f"[team] {what} failed: {error!r}")
        return fallback

        return fallback

My estimate is still **about 75–85**. There's no new result yet: the run is in a waiting phase, around minute 3–4 of its own clock.

Where the run stands:

I found one more flaw in my code while reading this: after the gap check, the run sits idle for about 3½ minutes, until about minute 6:30, even though every agent is done. My "stop waiting when everyone is finished" check runs only after that sleep. It costs time, not points: the follow-up still has up to 3½ minutes before the form starts at 12:30. It goes on the fix list.

**What decides the score:** the follow-up round, about minute 7–10, has to recover the metal index, the condition rules and, if missing, the two materials.
- Full recovery: about 95.
- Only the materials recovered: about 80.
- Nothing recovered: about 60–65.

Fixes for the next run, written and tested offline:
- Take the subjects the brief names as "X message", so all 9 topics get assigned.
- Release an agent only after a gap check finds its part complete.
- Skip the idle wait when every agent is done.
* Take the subjects the brief names as “X message”, so all 9 topics get assigned. what is that

That's about how the agent decides which mail messages to look for.

**The problem.** At the start, a "plan" step reads the brief and lists the mail topics: the subject words the agents search for in the mailbox, like "Devisenfixing" or "Rüstpools". The brief names those topics in two different ways:

1. **As a list of "Subject/sender" pairs:** "Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen". Since run #8, code reads these 6 straight from the brief, so they're never lost.
2. **Inside the rule sentences:** "Resolve that key in the latest **Konditionsregeln** message … from kalkulation@" and "select the latest exact-reference **Preisindizes** message from kalkulation@". These 2 were left entirely to the plan model.

In run #8 the model listed all of them. In run #9 it skipped these two and listed the tender reference "VG-2027-7093" as a topic instead. So no agent was assigned the condition rules or the metal index, and those two facts are missing in this run.

**The fix.** Code now also scans the brief for the pattern "<Capitalised word> message", plus the sender if one follows ("from kalkulation@"), and adds those words as topics. Run on the real brief, it now always yields all 8 named subjects plus the discount approval:
- Konditionsregeln (kalkulation@)
- Preisindizes (kalkulation@)
- Technikfreigabe (technik@)
- Verpackungstarife and Terminfreigabe (logistik@)
- Devisenfixing and Projektbonus (finanzen@)
- Rüstpools (kalkulation@)

It's generic: it reads the brief's wording at run time and contains no public values. A private brief that says "the latest X message" gets X as a topic the same way. Whatever the plan model forgets, every subject the brief names gets searched.

By "the model's choices" I meant the decisions the same model makes during the run: when to delegate, which requirement to look up, how to use the search. These vary from run to run with the same model and the same prompt. In run #8 it waited for the requirements and then delegated correctly; in run #10 it delegated at 0:39 with nothing to delegate yet.

That variance is why I keep moving such decisions from prompts into code checks. For the ERP, the next checks are:
- `delegate()` refuses a job until its catalogue group appears in another agent's records, so no helper starts before the requirements exist;
- it refuses a requirement no position uses;
- only running helpers count against the limit.

Then the same model can't make these mistakes, whatever it decides.

### Run #11 (`run_644527a83fe7f01d`): quality 100, 11:23 min

Every check full. What carried it:
- All 9 mail topics, from the brief's "Subject/sender" list and its "the latest X message" wording.
- The checklist, plus the gap check that re-sent agents after two wrong "absent" closes and one doubtful rate.
- ERP helpers with real requirement keys, and a gap agent for the last material.
- `record()` refusing values no page showed.
- A submitter without a way to give up.

The computed answer matched the hand-checked one at 8:49, with no follow-up needed.

Still seen in run #11, worth fixing later (none cost points):
- A gap agent recorded single-digit lead times it had probably not opened: one-digit numbers are not checked. The
  delivery commitment governed that position anyway. Idea: check "number + unit" phrases ("2 Wochen") against the
  pages that agent viewed.
- The ERP lead started a helper for a requirement no position uses; the job also named a used one, so the check let
  it through. Harmless.
- At one position the form's fields read empty after every fill for about 40 s, and the platform log showed the
  typing masked ("•••"); the submitter got through and the summary matched. A fallback that retypes with real
  keystrokes when a fill does not stick is written but not in the 100-point version
  (`out/pending-keystroke-fallback.txt`).
